messages:
Zara: FYI customer reported an export issue: their CSV contained raw vector columns by default. legal flagged it as a potential data leak for some datasets. Zara: the export modal currently has a tiny checkbox 'Include vectors' but it's unchecked in our current builds. customer says their CSV still had a vector field. Owen: yikes. can you share the CSV header they saw? Zara: headers: id,vector_1536,metadata,score,tags. they expected vector omitted. Carmen: product note: we intentionally allow vector export for research workflows but it must be opt-in and very explicit. we should (1) default to exclude vectors, (2) move 'Include vectors' into an advanced/confirm step with a short privacy warning, and (3) log export events with a flag. Noah: accessibility/UX: when we surface the privacy warning it must be associated with the checkbox via aria-describedby so screen readers read the brief warning. also keyboard users should be able to open the advanced options without a mouse (enter/space to toggle). Faye: copy suggestion for the advanced warning: "Warning: exporting raw vectors may contain sensitive information. Only export if you understand the data and have permission." Short tooltip: "Raw vectors may expose sensitive data - opt in intentionally." Luis: security/telemetry: add an audit event export.csv with metadata: include_vectors true/false, user_id, dataset_id. also add a retention policy for exported files. we'll need a quick compliance checklist for enterprise customers. Owen: UI pattern idea: collapse an "Advanced export" accordion. inside: a labeled checkbox \"Include raw vectors (opt-in)\" + linked privacy text and a required confirm checkbox \"I understand the risk\" before enabling the download button. Carmen: love that. microcopy for the confirm: \"I understand that exported vectors may contain sensitive or proprietary information and I have permission to export them.\" Make this SR-only? No, visible and required. Noah: technical aria snippet for the warning linkage: ```html
Exporting raw vectors may contain sensitive info. Confirm to proceed.
``` Noah: note: sr-only warning ensures screen reader users get the context; but also keep a visible short sentence so mouse users aren't surprised. maybe show visible short text and keep sr-only for extended explanation. Faye: small UX ask: add keyboard shortcut to toggle dense/compact rows. Suggested: "D" when focus is inside the preview list toggles density. But ensure no conflicts. Document in the tooltip: "Shortcut: D". Persist preference in user settings so power users don't re-toggle each session. Luis: from audit standpoint, toggling density isn't sensitive, but we should track exports and include_vectors usage. Also tie export events to the user's org export quota. Zara: QA will repro the reported CSV and confirm the default behavior. Carmen can we update Figma to show the advanced accordion + required confirm checkbox? also include the privacy copy. Carmen: will update Figma tokens and add the confirm flow. I'll include two visual states: compact rows + dense shortcut hint, and the advanced export modal with confirm. Owen: engineering notes: implement default exclude vectors, move CSV mapping to follow visible column order (exclude controls) and ensure JSONL exports have the same opt-in semantics. add unit tests for header order and include_vectors flag. Noah: accessibility checklist for the export modal: 1) aria-describedby on include checkbox, 2) focus trap inside modal, 3) visible required confirmation (with aria-invalid if not checked on download), 4) keyboard-accessible accordion. Luis: I'll prep an audit ticket and add required telemetry fields. Carmen, tag me when Figma is ready so we can review copy for legal. Faye: I'll prototype the dense toggle shortcut and a small preference persistence shim (localStorage + server-side opt-in). will share short demo. Zara: thanks — I'll file the bug, attach the offending CSV, and move QA tasks to this thread when ready. tagging @Owen @Carmen @Noah @Faye @Luis for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
